10.1002_aenm.202504343: There are few direct measurements of the coupling of electrochemical processes with mechanical stresses, especially when the applied stress is an independent control variable, and the stress is nearly uniform and on a planar interface. In this paper, we demonstrate a novel controlled interfacial stress platform for electrochemical‐mechanical (CISP‐ECM) coupling measurements at a single electrode/electrolyte interface. We realize this platform using a nanoindentation system and a sample composed of a thin‐film Li x V 2 O 5 electrode in a lateral configuration on a solid‐electrolyte substrate, and we report the coupling of applied stress and open‐circuit voltage (OCV). These measurements provide estimates of the partial molar volume of Li in the Li x V 2 O 5 thin‐film electrode at various lithiation states; the resulting mean volume expansion of 1.5% for x = 0.32 to 0.73 in Li x V 2 O 5 is consistent with literature crystallographic values. Our methods provide a means to measure the partial molar volume of lithium as a function of lithium content in electrode materials for both crystalline and amorphous electrode materials. In addition to solid‐state batteries, the CISP‐ECM platform is relevant to other areas where mechanical stresses can couple with variable‐composition electrode materials, such as wearable electronics, actuators, and iontronics.
10.1038_s41467-026-68903-5: Rechargeable magnesium batteries have emerged as a competitive next-generation energy storage technology owing to their abundant resources and inherent safety. The development of Mg batteries, especially regarding specific energy, has been compromised by the lack of high-performance positive electrodes. Here, we design an anion-receptor-mediated all-phenyl-complex electrolyte that enables the electrochemical cooperation between fluoride and magnesium, and develop a Mg | |FeO0.7F1.3 battery prototype. The anion receptor of tris(pentafluorophenyl)borane alters the chemical compositions of electrolyte and regulates its solvation structures via dipole-ion and dipole-dipole interactions with chloride-based ionic species and solvent molecules. The tailored electrolyte mitigates the chloride-originated anodic instability and upgrades the desolvation kinetics of cationic carriers. The dual-cation co-driven conversion-type Mg | |FeO0.7F1.3 batteries exhibit the high reversible capacities in a wide temperature range, delivering 354 mAh g⁻¹ at 25 °C and 177 mAh g⁻¹ at –20 °C. Moreover, the high reversibility over 500 cycles with a low capacity decay rate of 0.054% per cycle can be realized when confined to intercalation chemistry. This work provides an anion receptor-based electrolyte design strategy that expands positive material horizons for magnesium batteries to high-energy fluorides. The lack of high-energy positive materials hinders the development of magnesium metal batteries. Here, authors design an anion receptor-mediated electrolyte that enables the electrochemical cooperation between fluoride and magnesium, and develop a high-performance Mg | |FeO0.7F1.3 battery prototype.

10.1080_19475705.2026.2660859: Hydroclimatic seasonality can confound wetland disturbance monitoring by mimicking or masking fire effects. We present a reproducible, regime-aware framework to disentangle flood-pulse variability from disturbance in the northern Brazilian Pantanal (2020–2025). Using 75 Landsat 8 scenes, we derived NDVI and NBR time series and applied a two-stage unsupervised workflow: pixel-wise k-means (K = 4) to map distinct eco-spectral regimes, and clustering in NDVI–NBR space (K = 3) to define system states. The Severely Impacted state occupied ~18% of the record, concentrated in crisis years, with a maximum extent of ~36,700 km² and a persistence of 64 days during the 2024 drought. Validation confirmed strong negative associations between monthly mean NBR and independent fire metrics (MapBiomas: ρ = −0.72; VIIRS FRP: ρ = −0.79), contrasting with weaker associations for optical wetness proxies. A Random Forest baseline predicting NBR achieved high skill (R² = 0.87) but showed that predictability is driven largely by seasonal inertia rather than robust forecasting. Despite optical cloud gaps and spectral ambiguity between open water and severe burns, this open-source workflow provides a scalable, regime-conditioned baseline for consistent impact reporting in nonstationary floodplains.
10.1109_tte.2026.3655318: With the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), charging stations face increasing power demands, causing significant fluctuations in the utility grid. Battery energy storage systems (BESS) have emerged as effective solutions to mitigate fluctuations by managing power flow and levelling loads. However, the appropriate sizing of BESS and effective energy management are crucial for enhancing system techno-economics. This paper proposes a two-stage framework for optimal BESS sizing and real-time energy management in EV charging stations. In the first stage, a convex optimization algorithm determines the optimal BESS capacity and associated converter size by accounting for the stochastic nature of EV charging demand and detailed component models. The objective integrates investment cost, electricity cost, and penalties for peak-hour power consumption. The optimized BESS size is used for the second stage where a reinforcement learning (RL)-based energy management strategy is developed to achieve real-time decisions on charging prices of EV owners and power allocation between the utility grid and the BESS. To enhance learning efficiency, cyclical feature encoding is introduced to capture periodic patterns in electricity prices and EV arrivals. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed BESS sizing and energy management strategies, with a 17.6% cost reduction compared to a system without BESS. The RL-based energy management strategy enhances the net income of the charging station by up to 17.5% over a two-week period, outperforming traditional rule-based control methods.
